practiceQuestions.q: What was the term used by Akbar to describe his policy of universal peace and absolute tolerance towards all religions?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sulh-i Kul means 'universal peace' and formed the cornerstone of Akbar's religious and social policy, ensuring that all religions and schools of thought had freedom of expression. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year was the Ibadat Khana (House of Worship) constructed by Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri?
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar established the Ibadat Khana in 1575 at Fatehpur Sikri initially for religious discussions exclusively among Sunni Ulema, which later opened to scholars of all faiths. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: The 'Mahzar' of 1579 was primarily drafted by which prominent scholar and statesman?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Mahzar (Infallibility Decree) was drafted by Shaikh Mubarak (father of Abul Fazl and Faizi) in 1579, giving Akbar supreme judicial authority in interpreting religious matters if there was a conflict among ulema. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the official name or term used by contemporary historians like Abul Fazl for the spiritual order or discipleship promoted by Akbar?
practiceQuestions.sol: Contemporary records such as the Akbarnama refer to Akbar's order as 'Tauhid-i Ilahi' (Divine Monotheism). The term 'Din-i Ilahi' was popularized by later historians. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which social reform was enacted by Akbar to discourage child marriage and regulate the age of consent?
opts: Fixing minimum age of marriage for boys and girls
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar issued orders fixing the minimum age for marriage (16 for boys and 14 for girls) and prohibited marriages before puberty, alongside registering marriages with state officials. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did Akbar formally abolish the pilgrimage tax (Pilgrimage Tax on Hindus) across his empire?
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar abolished the pilgrimage tax in 1563, following his abolition of Jizya in 1564, as part of his early measures towards integrating his non-Muslim subjects. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary function of the 'Sadr-us-Sudur' during the early part of Akbar's reign?
opts: Head of ecclesiastical and charitable endowments department
Chief intelligence officer for border provinces
practiceQuestions.sol: The Sadr-us-Sudur was the head of religious and charitable endowments (Madad-i-Maash) and wielded immense power through patronage distributed to the orthodox ulema. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which Portuguese Jesuit priests were invited by Akbar to the imperial court to explain Christian theology?
opts: Father Antonio Monserrate and Rodolfo Acquaviva
Vasco da Gama and Pedro Alvares
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar invited Christian missionaries, notably the First Jesuit Mission consisting of Rudolf Acquaviva and Antonio Monserrate, to participate in religious discourses at Fatehpur Sikri. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What directive did Akbar issue regarding the practice of Sati?
opts: It was made compulsory for royal widows
It was permitted only with the explicit voluntary consent of the widow, prohibiting forcible immolation
It was completely banned with immediate death penalty for violators
It was ignored by state authorities as a private religious matter
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar regulated Sati by decreeing that no widow could be forced to commit Sati against her will, and state officials were instructed to personally verify the widow's consent. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, History of Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following Jain scholars was deeply honored by Akbar and given the title 'Jagat Guru'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar invited the eminent Jain scholar Acharya Hiravijaya Suri to his court from Gujarat. Impressed by his learning and asceticism, Akbar conferred upon him the title 'Jagat Guru'. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the promulgation of the 'Mahzar' (1579) alter the balance of power between the Mughal Emperor and the orthodox Islamic Ulema?
opts: It subordinated the Emperor to the collective fatwas of the leading qazis.
It elevated the Emperor to the position of 'Sultan-i Adil', giving him the ultimate arbiter role in religious interpretations when ulema differed.
It dismantled the Islamic character of the state and established Jainism as the state religion.
It abolished the Sharia completely across all civil and criminal jurisdictions.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Mahzar declared that if there were conflicting opinions among the ulema on religious points, Akbar—as 'Sultan-i Adil' (just ruler)—had the right to choose any interpretation that promoted public welfare, thereby clipping the wings of the orthodox ulema. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the structural significance of the Ibadat Khana debates in the evolution of Akbar's religious policy?
opts: They reinforced orthodox Sunni supremacy by silencing non-Muslim critics.
They exposed the bitter sectarian divisions and intolerance among the ulema, disillusioning Akbar with orthodox Islam.
They served exclusively as a platform for drafting the imperial revenue settlements.
They led to the immediate military conquest of the Deccan sultanates.
practiceQuestions.sol: When theologians of various sects (Sunni, Shia, Sufi, Hindu, Jain, Christian, Zoroastrian) squabbled bitterly and accused each other of heresy in the Ibadat Khana, Akbar realized the limitations of sectarian dogma, prompting his shift toward 'Sulh-i Kul'. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Akbar's administrative reforms regarding 'Madad-i-Maash' grants systematically curtail the corruption of the Sadr office?
opts: By transferring the power of granting tax-free land exclusively to corrupt local zamindars.
By ordering verification, reducing grants by half for many holders, and curbing the arbitrary patronage powers of the Sadr.
By replacing land grants entirely with payments in foreign gold currency.
By prohibiting all religious endowments to Muslims while doubling grants to Europeans.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Sadr office had been plagued by bribery and nepotism in distributing Madad-i-Maash (tax-free land to scholars and holy men). Akbar instituted strict checks, reduced grants pending verification, and curbed the autonomous unchecked power of the Sadr. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the philosophical core of 'Tauhid-i Ilahi' or Din-i Ilahi as established by Akbar?
opts: A rigid dogmatic theology based strictly on Hanafi jurisprudence.
An eclectic moral code emphasizing loyalty to the emperor as spiritual guide, peace, asceticism, and tolerance of all creeds.
A military pact exclusively designed to conquer Central Asia.
An economic alliance with European trading companies.
practiceQuestions.sol: Din-i Ilahi was not a new religion with holy books or prophets, but a moral and spiritual order of disciples bound to the Emperor. It promoted virtues like truth, compassion, abstaining from meat, and absolute loyalty to the sovereign. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Akbar encourage the translation of Sanskrit works like the Mahabharata, Ramayana, and Upanishads into Persian (creating the 'Makhatab Khana')?
opts: To destroy Hindu texts and replace them with fabricated anti-religious literature.
To bridge the cultural and intellectual gap between diverse communities and foster mutual understanding under Sulh-i Kul.
To prepare a blueprint for heavy taxation on temple lands.
To export Indian classical literature exclusively to Ottoman Turkey for commercial gain.
To train Islamic clerics in Sanskrit so they could argue against Hindu philosophies.

The establishment of the translation bureau (Maktab Khana) reflected Akbar's intellectual curiosity and his deliberate policy of reducing religious friction by familiarizing the Muslim elite with Hindu philosophical traditions and vice versa. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Akbar's abolition of Jizya (1564) impact the political architecture of the Mughal Empire?
opts: It caused an immediate financial bankruptcy of the imperial treasury.
It alienated the Muslim mansabdars, leading to immediate civil war.
It dismantled theocratic discrimination, helping build a broad-based ruling class integrating Rajputs and other non-Muslims.
It forced the Hindu population to pay double land revenue instead.
practiceQuestions.sol: The abolition of Jizya was a masterstroke of political integration. By removing discriminatory taxation based on religion, Akbar secured the unflinching loyalty of Hindu rajas (like Rajputs) and laid the foundation of a secular imperial state. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the attitude of orthodox Muslim chroniclers, such as Abdul Qadir Badauni, towards Akbar's socio-religious initiatives?
opts: Severe condemnation, viewing his innovations as deviations from orthodox Islam and a betrayal of Islamic law.
Complete indifference, as they were unaware of court policies.
Active participation as enthusiastic members of Din-i Ilahi.
practiceQuestions.sol: Badauni, in his Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh, bitterly criticized Akbar, accusing him of abandoning Islamic principles, showing disrespect to the Prophet, and favoring Hindus and heretics. His writings provide an essential counter-perspective to Abul Fazl's eulogies. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Akbar reform social customs regarding dietary habits, gambling, and prostitution within his empire?
opts: He legalized prostitution and taxed gambling dens heavily.
He regulated consumption of meat by limiting slaughter days, restricted gambling, and segregated prostitutes in a designated suburb called Shaitanpura.
He enforced strict vegetarianism on the entire imperial population.
He ignored these social evils completely as personal freedoms.
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar instituted moral police regulations. He restricted meat eating on certain holy days, regulated wine consumption for medicinal use, checked gambling, and segregated prostitutes outside city walls in 'Shaitanpura' (Devil's town) with registered superintendents. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of Akbar's interactions with Zoroastrian (Parsi) high priests, such as Dastur Meherjee Rana?
opts: It led to the adoption of sacred fire worship and sun worship practices in the imperial court.
It was purely a diplomatic mission to secure naval trade with Persia.
It resulted in the persecution of Zoroastrians in Gujarat.
It was meant to convert Parsi priests to Sunni Islam.
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar deeply respected Zoroastrianism, learning about it from Dastur Meherjee Rana. This influenced his adoption of sun and fire veneration as symbols of divine light, which were incorporated into his daily court rituals. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of Mughal governance, what was the underlying political utility of Akbar's eclectic religious policies?
opts: To appease European colonial powers and prevent naval blockades.
To forge a unified imperial ruling elite transcending ethnic and religious cleavages, cementing loyalty to the centralized Mughal state.
To facilitate the smooth collection of religious tithes from foreign pilgrims.
To dismantle the mansabdari system in favor of hereditary feudal fiefs.
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar recognized that ruling a vast, multi-religious subcontinent required moving beyond narrow sectarianism. Sulh-i Kul and social reforms served to bind diverse ethnic groups (Turani, Irani, Afghan, Rajput, Indian Muslim) into a cohesive imperial ruling class. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, History of Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Akbar's religious policies:
1. The Ibadat Khana, initially restricted to Sunni theologians, was later thrown open to members of all religions including Christians, Zoroastrians, Hindus, and Jains.
2. The 'Mahzar' signed in 1579 gave Akbar absolute authority to issue binding fatwas on all secular and administrative matters while relinquishing all control over religious interpretations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Ibadat Khana was opened to all faiths after bitter disputes among the Sunni ulema disillusioned Akbar. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Mahzar gave Akbar supreme authority specifically in interpreting religious matters when ulema disagreed, not administrative matters alone, and it did not relinquish religious control. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding social reforms initiated by Emperor Akbar:
1. He completely banned the custom of Sati without any exceptions throughout his empire.
2. He raised the age of marriage and instituted regulations making the registration of marriages mandatory.
3. He prohibited the enslavement of people captured during military campaigns.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Akbar did not completely ban Sati; he regulated it by prohibiting forcible immolation and requiring voluntary consent. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Akbar fixed minimum ages for marriage, registered marriages, and banned the practice of forcing prisoners of war into slavery. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Sulh-i Kul':
1. It was conceived as a purely military strategy to subdue recalcitrant Afghan chieftains.
2. It implied a policy of universal peace and tolerance, treating all religious communities fairly without discrimination.
3. Abul Fazl described it as the cornerstone of enlightened imperial governance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Sulh-i Kul was a socio-religious and political philosophy of peace and tolerance, not a military strategy. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: It formed the basis of Akbar's pluralistic governance, championed by Abul Fazl in the Akbarnama and Ain-i Akbari. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the institutional reforms of Akbar:
1. Akbar abolished the pilgrimage tax on Hindus in 1563 and the Jizya in 1564.
2. The 'Sadr-us-Sudur' department's authority was systematically checked by Akbar to curb corruption in the distribution of Madad-i-Maash grants.
3. Akbar prohibited cow slaughter entirely across the entire Mughal Empire under penalty of death.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Akbar abolished the pilgrimage tax in 1563 and Jizya in 1564, and he reformed the Sadr office to halt corruption in tax-free land grants. Statement 3 is incorrect: While Akbar placed restrictions on cow slaughter to respect Hindu sentiments, he did not institute a universal empire-wide total ban with death penalty. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the intellectual and translation activities under Akbar:
1. The 'Maktab Khana' was established exclusively to translate Greek philosophical treatises into Arabic.
2. Eminent Sanskrit scholars like Badrayana and various Jain monks were welcomed at Akbar's court for philosophical discourses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Maktab Khana (translation bureau) was established primarily to translate Sanskrit classics like Mahabharata, Ramayana, and Upanishads into Persian. Statement 2 is correct: Akbar welcomed Sanskrit scholars and Jain monks like Hiravijaya Suri to his court. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Din-i Ilahi' or 'Tauhid-i Ilahi':
1. It was a compulsory state religion that every Mughal military commander was forced to adopt under pain of execution.
2. It had no sacred scriptures, priesthood, or holy books, functioning instead as an elite order of discipleship.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Din-i Ilahi was entirely voluntary and had very few adherents (around 18 prominent courtiers including Birbal). Statement 2 is correct: It lacked a formal priesthood, scriptures, or dogma, functioning as a moral order of loyalty to the Emperor. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, History of Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Akbar's relations with the orthodox Ulema:
1. Akbar sought to break the monopoly of orthodox Sunni ulema over state religious policy through institutional measures like the Mahzar and the Ibadat Khana debates.
2. Most orthodox ulema supported Akbar's social reforms, especially those regarding women's rights and freedom of expression.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Akbar challenged the orthodox ulema's monopoly through the Mahzar and exposing their intolerance in the Ibadat Khana. Statement 2 is incorrect: The orthodox ulema fiercely opposed Akbar's social reforms (such as age of marriage and regulation of Sati) and religious liberalism, viewing them as un-Islamic. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the socio-cultural environment under Akbar:
1. Akbar permitted the construction of new temples and churches while ensuring protection to minority religious practices.
2. The Jesuit missions dispatched from Goa were barred from holding public religious debates with Muslim theologians in front of the Emperor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Akbar allowed non-Muslims to repair old temples, construct new ones, and practice their faiths openly. Statement 2 is incorrect: Jesuit priests actively participated in religious discourses and debates with Muslim, Hindu, and Jain scholars in Akbar's presence. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the historical sources for Akbar's religious policy:
1. Abul Fazl's 'Akbarnama' and 'Ain-i Akbari' present a highly favorable, institutional justification of Akbar's policies and Sulh-i Kul.
2. Abdul Qadir Badauni's 'Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh' offers a critical, orthodox theological critique of Akbar's departure from Islamic orthodoxy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Abul Fazl was Akbar's court historian and chief ideologue who championed Sulh-i Kul in official chronicles, whereas Badauni wrote secretly from an aggrieved orthodox Sunni perspective, providing a vital counter-narrative. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Akbar's economic and social regulations:
1. Akbar levied heavy taxes on the consumption of wine and completely banned its sale for all purposes including medical use.
2. He tried to discourage child marriage by fixing minimum age limits for boys and girls.
3. He established separate designated quarters outside city limits for beggars and entertainers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: While Akbar regulated wine sale and consumption, permits were issued for its purchase for medicinal purposes under strict supervision, and it was not totally banned for all medical uses. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Akbar fixed minimum ages for marriage and regulated vagrancy and segregation of certain social classes. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]
